captions.short_caption: Total Solar Eclipse pictured from Bangladesh
captions.caption: This image represents the total solar eclipse as observed from Kurigram in Bangladesh. Solar eclipses occur when the moon, as seen from earth, passes in front of the Sun. The moon is much smaller than the Sun, it is closer by the night amount that the angular diameters of the Sun and moon are almost the same (~approximately 1/2 a fingertip). Therefore, the moon can cover up the Sun's disk when it passes directly between the Sun and the Earth. The ring of light around the black circle is called the corona.
captions.alt_text: The Moon appears as a black circle, blocking light from the Sun. A faint glow from the Solar corona surrounds the Moon.

results.file_title: Total Solar Eclipse from Casper, Wyoming, USA

captions.file_title: Total Solar Eclipse from Casper, Wyoming, USA
captions.short_caption: Total Solar Eclipse from Casper, Wyoming, USA
captions.caption:
This video shows the total solar eclipse of the 21st of August 2017 observed from Casper, Wyoming, USA by a team of astronomers from the European Space Agency (ESA). This video has been sped up considerably, in reality the moment of totality lasted just under two and a half minutes while the time from the Moon first appearing to obscure the Sun until the Sun was completely unobscured was two hours and 48 minutes.

Before the eclipse we can see several sunspots on the Sun. The Moon moves across the Sun, covering the whole solar disk visible from the point on the Earth this video was taken from. At totality we can see the diffuse solar corona which is normally outshone by the bright solar disk. 

Note that while edges of the Sun appear brighter just before and just after totality, this is due to exposure time of the camera being adjusted to make the features visible at totality more obvious. Towards the end of the video some thin cloud begins to affect the observations.
captions.alt_text: The Moon moves from top right to bottom right, covering then uncovering the Sun. At totality wispy features surround the Sun
